In
FA No. 12 of 2022, FA No. 15 of 2022, FA No. 16 of 2022, FA No. 17 of 2022, FA No. 18 of 
2022, FA No. 19 of 2022, FA No. 20 of 2022, FA No. 23 of 2022, FA No. 24 of 2022, FA No. 
25 of 2022, FA No. 33 of 2022, FA No. 34 of 2022, FA No. 37 of 2022, FA No. 39 of 2022
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned counsel for the 
appellant.
2. Mr. I.P. Kohli, learned Standing Counsel for the 
State.
3. Mr. Ajay Kumar, learned counsel for the 
respondent through V.C.
4. Mr. Tarun Lakhera and Mr. Shivanand Bhatt, 
learned counsel for the respondents in the connected 
appeals.
5. All these first appeals have been preferred against 
the impugned award passed by the Land Acquisition 
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Authority (LARRA), 
Uttarakhand, whereby the appellant herein Rail Vikas 
Nigam Ltd. was directed to give 12% per annum simple 
interest on the awarded amount and to provide the 
employment to one of the dependants of the family 
whose land was acquired.
6. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that so 
far as the quantum of compensation and the direction for 
giving 12% per annum interest on the awarded amount is 
concerned RVNL the present appellant are not pressing 
appeal and to that extent appeal be permitted to be 
withdrawn; however, instant appeals are being pressed
only in respect of the limited issue of giving employment 
to one of the dependants of the family whose land was 
acquired in lieu of Rs. 5 lakhs the additional 
compensation.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the 
possession has already been handed over to the Rail 
Vikas Nigam Ltd. and since the appellant is not pressing 
the appeal in respect of the quantum of compensation 
and the amount towards the interest and the instant 
appeals are being pressed only for the limited issue, 
therefore, for the limited issue the appeals be admitted by 
condoning the delay. 8. Learned counsel for the respondents have not 
raised any objection on the delay condonation 
application.
9. Learned Standing Counsel Mr. I.P. Kohli and Mr. 
Tarun Lakhera, learned counsel for the claimants submits 
that they have no objection if the appellant are not 
pressing the appeal in respect of the quantum of 
compensation and the interest.
10. Accordingly, the instant first appeals are dismissed 
as withdrawn so far it relates to the quantum of 
compensation and interest component. All these appeals 
are admitted only to a limited issue of giving 
employment to the dependant of the family whose land 
were acquired.
11. Learned counsel for the appellant Mr. V.K. 
Kaparuwan also submits since the instant first appeals 
are only admitted to the limited issue of giving 
employment and it is purely legal issue, therefore, there 
is no need to summon the record.
12. In FA 23 of 2022 the substitution application moved 
by the learned counsel for the appellant is allowed.
13. Let the amended memo of parties be filed within a 
week.
14. It has been apprised by the learned counsel for the 
parties that some of the claimants have received the 
amount of compensation but some of them have not 
received.
15. In such view of the matter, the Collector, Pauri 
Garhwal is directed to do the needful for disbursement of 
the amount of compensation along with interest. 
16. It is made clear that while disbursing the amount 
towards the interest the Collector shall ensure that the 
interest will be payable at the rate of 12% per annum only 
till the date of depositing the amount of compensation.
17. It is made clear that receiving the amount of 
compensation and the interest by any of the claimants 
will not affect their right to get the employment which 
infact is the subject matter of the instant first appeals.
18. Let the copy of this order be handed over to Mr. 
I.P. Kohli, learned Standing Counsel for necessary 
compliance.
19. List all these appeal on 22.09.2025 for final hearing.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 16.09.2025
PR

FA No. 12 of 2022, FA No. 15 of 2022, FA No. 16 of 2022, FA No. 17 of 2022, FA No. 18 of 
2022, FA No. 19 of 2022, FA No. 20 of 2022, FA No. 23 of 2022, FA No. 24 of 2022, FA No. 
25 of 2022, FA No. 28 of 2022, FA No. 29 of 2022, FA No. 33 of 2022, FA No. 34 of 2022, FA 
No. 37 of 2022, FA No. 38 of 2022, FA No. 39 of 2022
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned counsel for the 
appellant.
2. Mr. I.P. Kohli, learned Standing Counsel for the 
State.
3. Mr. Siddhartha Sah with Mr. Ajay Kumar, learned 
counsel for the respondent.
4. Mr. Tarun Lakhera, learned counsel for the 
respondents in the connected First Appeals.
5. All these bunch of First Appeals are confined to a 
limited issue of giving employment to the members of the 
affected families by virtue of Entry 4 of Schedule 2 Act 
No. 30 of 2013.
6. As per Entry 4 of Schedule 2 of Right to Fair 
Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, 
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, it is 
mandatory upon the appropriate Government to ensure 
that the affected families are provided three options i.e. 
Option (a), Option (b) and Option (c). The reference court 
by the order impugned observed that each of the options 
are binding upon the appropriate Government and to 
choose a particular option is completely a prerogative of 
the affected family.
7. Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned counsel for the 
appellant argued that the Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd., in short, 
RVNL, is only an Executing Agency of the Central 
Government and here in respect of the project the 
appropriate Government is the Central Government, 
therefore, the options as per Entry 4 of Schedule 2 can 
only be implemented by the appropriate Government i.e. 
the Central Government and not by the Executing 
Agency. He submits that the project is a time bound 
project and after implementation of the project it will be 
handed over to the concerned Ministry for its operational
and maintenance and, therefore, by virtue of Entry 4 of 
Schedule 2 r/w Section 31 of Act No. 30 of 2013 only the 
appropriate Government, the Central Government, can  implement options and here in this case since the affected 
families opt for employment, therefore, such employment 
can only be offered by the appropriate Government i.e. 
the Central Government and not by the Executing 
Agency the RVNL.
8. I found force on the submission of learned counsel 
for the appellant that even if the affected families opted 
for job even then job can only be offered by the 
appropriate Government i.e. the Central Government that 
too on completion and handing over the project.
9. Learned counsel for the respondents submits that 
most of the affected families have opted for job but there 
are some affected families, who opt for compensation in 
lieu of employment.
10. Let the learned counsel for the respondents may 
get instructions from their client.
11. List this matter on 25.09.2025 on top of Board along 
with FA Nos. 31, 32 and 229 of 2022 and the Chief Project 
Manager (CPM) may join the proceeding through V.C. 
after getting necessary instructions from the appropriate 
Government with regard to implementation of option of 
providing job to the affected families.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 23.09.2025
PR

FA No. 12 of 2022, FA No. 15 of 2022, FA No. 16 of 2022, FA No. 17 of 2022, FA No. 18 of 
2022, FA No. 19 of 2022, FA No. 20 of 2022, FA No. 23 of 2022, FA No. 24 of 2022, FA No. 
25 of 2022, FA No. 28 of 2022, FA No. 29 of 2022, FA No. 33 of 2022, FA No. 34 of 2022, FA 
No. 37 of 2022, FA No. 38 of 2022, FA No. 39 of 2022
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned counsel for the 
appellant.
2. Mr. I.P. Kohli, learned Standing Counsel for the 
State.
3. Mr. Siddhartha Sah with Mr. Ajay Kumar, learned 
counsel for the respondent.
4. Mr. Tarun Lakhera and Mr. Shivanand Bhatt, 
learned counsel for the respondents in the connected First 
Appeals.
5. All these First Appeals are admitted only for 
determination of limited issue giving employment in lieu
of compensation of Rs. 5 lakhs. As per Entry 4 of 
Schedule 2 of Act No. 30 of 2013. Entry 4 of Schedule 2 
provides that the appropriate Government shall ensure 
that the affected families are provided with the options 
i.e. Option (a), (b) and (c). As per Section 3(e)(v) in 
relation to the acquisition of land the Central 
Government is the appropriate Government.
Section 31 under Chapter V of Act No. 30 of 2013, 
which pertains to Rehabilitation and Resettlement award 
makes a provisions for Rehabilitation and Resettlement 
award for the affected families by the Collector. Sub￾section (2) of Section 31 of Act No. 30 of 2013 provides 
that the Rehabilitation and Resettlement award shall 
include the details of mandatory employment to be 
provided to the members of the affected families.
6. On 28.04.2018 the Collector issue an award by 
observing that there will be a separate award for 
Rehabilitation and Resettlement as per Schedule 2 of 
Schedule 3. The award under Schedule 2 and 3 are not on 
record. Let the appellant may file it by the next date.
7. These First Appeals were admitted on 16.09.2025 
for considering the limited issue for implementation of 
Entry 4 of Schedule 2 of Act No. 30 of 2013. Since, all 
these appeals are admitted, therefore, following points 
for determination are being formulated: i. Whether the options provided in terms of Entry 4 
of Schedule 2 of Act No. 30 of 2013 is prerogative 
of the claimant to choose one of them?
ii. Whether the appropriate Government for the 
implementation of the options in terms of Entry 4 
of Schedule 2 of Act No. 30 of 2013 is the Central 
Government or the RVNL and at what stage the 
job should be offered to the affected families?
8. As per definition clause i.e. Section 3(e)(v) of Act 
No. 30 of 2013 prima-facie it appears that the appropriate 
Government is the Central Government, therefore for 
proper adjudication to these First Appeals the Central 
Government, the Ministry of Railway Govt. of India is 
permitted to be arrayed as one of the respondent for 
which learned counsel for the appellant is given liberty to 
move an appropriate application.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant is directed to 
implead concerned Ministry as one of the respondent 
during course of the day.
10. In the meantime, the appellant RVNL is directed to 
send the requisition to the appropriate Government for 
the purposes of implementation of the options given in 
terms of Entry 4 Schedule 2 of Act No. 30 of 2013.
11. Till then the execution proceeding, if any, shall 
remain in abeyance.
12. It is also further made clear that those affected 
families who have opted for the amount of compensation 
in lieu of employment are permitted to withdraw the 
amount of compensation and if such an application is 
moved by any affected family or their member, the 
Collector shall release the amount with interest without 
any delay.
13. In compliance to the previous order Mr. Ajit Singh 
Yadav, the Chief Project Manager of RVNL is present in 
court in order to assist. For the time being, the personal 
appearance of the official concerned is exempted.
14. Put up all these appeals on 14.10.2025.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 25.09.2025
PR

FA No. 31 of 2022, FA No. 18 of 2022, FA No. 32 of 2022, FA No. 229 of 2022
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan, learned counsel for the 
appellant.
2. Mr. Siddhartha Sah, learned counsel for the 
private respondents.
3. Mr. Lalit Sharma, learned Deputy Solicitor General 
for India/Indian Railway.
4. All these appeals have been filed by the Rail Vikas 
Nigam Ltd. against the order of reference, whereby, the 
reference court directed to the appellant to offer an 
employment in lieu of the additional compensation of Rs. 
5 lakhs. On the previous date the State was directed to 
classify the cases in which the claimants have received an 
additional amount of compensation i.e. Rs. 5 lakhs and to 
segregate those cases in which the claimants are seeking 
employment in lieu of the additional compensation.
5. Mr. I.P. Kohli, who represents the State, examined
and classified and submits that except in four cases in 
other appeals the claimants already accepted the 
additional amount of compensation of Rs. 5 lakhs.
6. Once the claimants accepted the amount towards 
additional compensation of Rs. 5 lakhs in lieu of 
employment, therefore, they cannot claim further to get 
an employment, however this issue are involved in other 
set of appeals which are now delinked.
7. In such view of the matter, since as per the 
mandate of the Act two options have been given by the 
Corporation either to accept the additional amount of 
compensation of Rs. 5 lakhs or to get employment, 
therefore, this is completely a prerogative of the 
complainant to opt for one offer.
8. Mr. V.K. Kaparuwan apprise to this court that 
infact RVNL is an executing agency of the Ministry of 
Railways and after completion they have to handover 
entire project to the Ministry of Railways for its 
maintenance and functioning and as such employment 
can be offered by the Ministry of Railways.
9. In such view of the matter since Mr. Lalit Sharma  have not received any instructions, in such view of the 
matter, last opportunity is given to get the instructions or 
to file an affidavit positively within ten days.
10. Put up this matter on 03.01.2026.
 
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 15.12.2025
PR
